quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: To swerve correctly:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to turn. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you avoid the hazard.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you out of other drivers' blind spots and away from road hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight when riding in fog. Do not use high beams near other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing down sooner than you would normally.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle will respond more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation works best for group riding, but switch to single-file when going through curves, turns, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: If a rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and have every rider travel at their own pace.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them ride ahead. Meet up at a planned location later.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately and then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever firmly with all four fingers, gradually applying more force.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In New Hampshire, a legal drinking age adult with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: You should try to avoid hitting an animal if it is safe to do so. However, when riding in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to avoid an animal can cause a crash with another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is especially helpful when riding through areas where dangers may appear.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, you should use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these surfaces are often slippery.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you must stop quickly in a curve, first straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten your motorcycle, apply the brakes slowly and gradually, reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on a good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation usually works best for groups riding together because it keeps riders close while giving each rider space. A single-file formation is better when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which action helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Do not use the center of the lane. Instead, follow the tire tracks left by other cars. Watch for oil spots, loose gravel, and other hazards that make surfaces slippery.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Drinking and driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Does not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may lose balance and interfere with the operator's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake hard in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel for maximum stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when turning left on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When there is a lot of traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy. You do not need to increase distance when you have a clear view ahead.

questions.question: What is a limitation of motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They cannot replace a face shield.
They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
They do not protect against items from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not an adequate substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you avoid doing on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Braking quickly
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to accelerate out of a wobble.
